rules.title: Unconscionable Rent Increase
rules.requirement: A residential rent increase may be treated as unconscionable if it is exceedingly harsh or unreasonable, exceeds the increase in the landlord’s expenses, and is not comparable to rents charged at similar properties. For properties with a redevelopment agreement or financial agreement, rent that exceeds the approved pro-forma is per se unconscionable.
rules.key_value: Exceedingly harsh or unreasonable; exceeds landlord’s expenses; not comparable to similar properties

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to residential properties including market and unsubsidized units; does not apply to units statutorily exempt from rent control under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1-84.6 or units controlled and governed by HUD.
coverage.summary: Covers residential properties, including market and unsubsidized units, except statutory rent-control-exempt units and HUD-controlled units.

rules.exemptions: Residential units statutorily exempt from Rent Control pursuant to N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1-84.6 and units controlled and governed by HUD are excluded.
rules.interaction: The definition states that it does not apply to units statutorily exempt from rent control under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1-84.6 or to units controlled and governed by HUD.
rules.quoted_span: UNCONSCIONABLE RENT — Shall mean any rental increase for residential properties including but not limited to market and unsubsidized units, whose rental increases are exceedingly harsh or unreasonable that exceed the increase in the landlord’s expenses; and is not comparable to rents charged at similar properties.
